---
name: software-design
description: Applies principles from "A Philosophy of Software Design" to architecture, module and API boundaries, and consequential refactors. Use for architecture planning, module or API design, design review, or diagnosing shallow modules, information leakage, and pass-through layers.
---

# Software Design

Apply these principles when architecture or abstraction quality is a material part of the task.

## Two Modes

### Writing New Code

Apply these principles in order of impact.

#### Think strategically

Invest in design instead of stopping when the code first works. Produce a clean design that works, and spend 10–20% of the effort on design improvements.

#### Create deep modules

Each module should provide powerful functionality behind a simple interface. A few deep methods beat many shallow ones. Ask whether the interface is simpler than the implementation.

#### Hide information

Each module should encapsulate design decisions that remain invisible through its interface. If one decision appears in several modules, reorganize the code until that decision has one home.

#### Make interfaces general-purpose

Design an interface broad enough to support current uses while keeping its functionality focused. Ask for the simplest interface that covers every current need.

#### Give each layer a different abstraction

Adjacent layers should operate at different abstraction levels. Remove pass-through methods that delegate with the same signature.

#### Pull complexity downwards

Handle complexity inside the module instead of pushing it to callers. A simple interface matters more than a simple implementation.

#### Define errors out of existence

Redefine APIs so avoidable error conditions cannot arise. Mask low-level exceptions and consolidate their handling. Reserve crashes for unrecoverable failures.

#### Design it twice

Consider at least two radically different approaches before committing. Compare their strengths and costs. Apply this comparison to interfaces and implementations, then consider the broader system decomposition.

#### Name precisely

Names should create a clear mental image of an entity's purpose. Avoid vague choices such as `data`, `result`, `info`, or `tmp`. Name booleans with predicates such as `isConnected` instead of a state label such as `status`.

#### Be consistent

Use the same name for the same purpose everywhere. Reuse established coding patterns and conventions. Consistency reduces the reader's cognitive work.

#### Make code obvious

Code is obvious when a reader's first guess about its behaviour is correct. Choose precise names and follow established patterns. Use whitespace to expose structure, and comment only where the code cannot explain itself.

#### Write comments first

Write interface comments before implementation. A method that needs a long descriptive comment has a complex interface and should be redesigned. Comments should preserve information that code cannot represent.

### Reviewing Existing Code

Scan for these red flags in the listed order.

#### Shallow modules

Look for interfaces as complex as their implementations, many trivial methods, or classes with little functionality.

#### Information leakage

Find design decisions repeated across modules. A change to one detail should not require coordinated edits across several classes.

#### Temporal decomposition

Check for code organized around operation order instead of information hiding, such as separate read and write classes for one format.

#### Pass-through methods

Flag methods that only call another method with the same signature, especially when delegation accounts for half or more of a class's methods.

#### Overexposure

A common operation should not force callers to understand rare features. Default information that callers should not have to provide.

#### Conjoined methods

Flag a method when understanding it requires reading another method's implementation.

#### Repetition

Find non-trivial code patterns duplicated in several places.

#### Vague or hard-to-pick names

Flag names broad enough to describe many entities. Difficulty finding a precise name often means the entity has too many responsibilities.

#### Comment problems

Find comments that restate the code or expose implementation details in interface documentation. Long, complicated descriptions may reveal a poor abstraction.

#### Special-general mixture

Keep specialized use-case code out of a general-purpose mechanism.

#### Nonobvious code

Flag behaviour that a quick reading cannot reveal, including surprising side effects.

#### Too many exceptions

Look for exceptions the caller cannot handle and error paths longer than the normal path. Redefine operations when doing so can eliminate error conditions.

For the full checklist, read `references/red-flags.md`.

## References

`references/principles.md` covers all 15 design principles. It includes examples and techniques, along with the reasoning behind each principle. Read it when applying a specific principle or when deeper context is needed.

`references/red-flags.md` organizes every red flag by category. Read it during code review to check systematically for design problems.

# Frontend Software Design Review (A Philosophy of Software Design lens)

Scope: `/Users/user/projects/yinshi/frontend/src` only. `frontend/dist` and `node_modules` were excluded.
Method: full reads of the ten largest source files plus targeted greps across all 56 non-test modules. `npx tsc --noEmit` was run and passes with no errors. No files were modified.

Note on inputs: the task referenced `/Users/user/projects/yinshi/plan.md` and `/Users/user/projects/yinshi/progress.md`. Neither file exists in the repository. `docs/plans/` and `code_reviews/` were checked instead for context.

---

## 1. Quantitative summary

| File | Lines | `useState` calls | `useEffect` calls | Component functions | Raw `/api/...` string literals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `components/Sidebar.tsx` | 1203 | 26 | 7 | 5 | 13 |
| `pages/Settings.tsx` | 968 | 24 | 4 | 5 | 4 |
| `components/CloudRunnerSection.tsx` | 837 | 17 | 2 | 2 | 4 |
| `components/WorkspaceInspector.tsx` | 757 | 12 | 4 | 4 | 7 |
| `pages/Session.tsx` | 668 | 12 | 7 | 1 | 4 |
| `api/client.ts` | 579 | -- | -- | -- | 5 |
| `runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts` | 555 | -- | -- | -- | 2 |
| `components/ChatView.tsx` | 400 | 5 | 1 | 1 | 0 |

Cross-cutting counts:

- 60 raw `/api/...` URL literals across 16 modules; 32 of them live directly in `components/` and `pages/`.
- 27 references to `window.yinshiDesktop` across 9 non-test modules.
- 29 direct inspections of `RuntimeRef.location` across 9 non-test modules.
- 5 independent copies of `RESOURCE_ID_PATTERN = /^[0-9a-f]{32}$/`.
- 3 independent base64url encoders.
- 4 call sites fetching `GET /api/settings/runner`, with 4 different definitions of "this runner is usable".
- 3 independent `formatTimestamp` implementations.

---

## 2. Findings

### F1. Sidebar.tsx is a four-responsibility god module (severity: high)

`components/Sidebar.tsx:166-498` (`Sidebar`), `:500-806` (`RepoSection`), `:808-953` (`WorkspaceItem`), `:955-1203` (`ImportForm`) hold 26 `useState` calls and 7 effects in one file. The distinct responsibilities are:

1. **Multi-runtime discovery and fan-out fetch.** `Sidebar.loadRepos` at `:188-259` probes the hosted runtime (`:200-217`), probes the BYOC runner (`:218-243`), aggregates three repository lists, and computes a per-location error banner list (`locationErrors`, `:185`).
2. **GitHub App installation state and OAuth callback query-string handling.** `githubNoticeFromSearch` at `:97-129`, `loadGitHubInstallations` at `:261-281`, and the URL-rewriting effect at `:283-308`.
3. **Repository-level settings editing.** `RepoSection` owns an AGENTS.md draft editor with its own save/cancel/notice/error state machine at `:522-525` and `:589-628`, plus a 60-line textarea form at `:695-757`.

## 3. Direct answers to the five questions

**Q1. God components.** Confirmed for all three. `Sidebar.tsx` holds 6 responsibilities (F1) and 26 `useState` calls. `Settings.tsx` holds 5 (account display, desktop profile management, FileVault status, runtime-location selection, tab routing) plus the `ProviderCard` sub-god with 15 `useState` calls covering 3 auth mechanisms and a 600-iteration poll loop (F3). `CloudRunnerSection.tsx` holds 4 (provisioning, Noise pairing, health probing, BYOC repository CRUD) with 17 `useState` calls (F4).

**Q2. Is `api/client.ts` deep or shallow?** Neither, precisely. It exposes 14 public members: 6 verbs on `api`, 6 on `hostedApi`, `streamPrompt`, `cancelSession` (plus `ApiError`, `normalizeEvent`, and 25 wire interfaces). It is not a per-endpoint wrapper. Its abstraction value is real but thin: it centralises credentials, CSRF header, 401 redirect, error normalisation, and 204 handling -- that is genuine, and `_readApiError`/`_normalizeErrorPayload` (`:256-320`) are properly deep. The failures are (a) four redeclarations of the same 6-verb signature across two files, (b) URL-space overexposure (60 literals, 32 in UI code), (c) a hidden path-membership routing rule (`:317-321`), and (d) roughly 90 lines of unreachable SSE code. See F8.

**Q3. Does `runtime/` leak transport details into components?** Yes, though the abstraction itself is well designed. `RuntimeTransport` (`runtimeTransport.ts:36-44`) is the right interface and `useRuntimeResource` is the right entry point -- `Session.tsx` proves it works. But "which runtime am I talking to" is decided in at least 6 places (F5), and `RuntimeRef.location` is inspected 29 times across 9 modules, including presentation code that should not care: `WorkspaceInspector.tsx:321` hides the download link for `byoc`, `Sidebar.tsx:516` collapses BYOC repos by default, `promptStream.ts:174` picks a poll delay by location, `piCommandsCache.ts:22` keys the cache by location. The first two are UI policy driven by a transport detail; they should be capability flags on the transport (`transport.supportsDirectDownload`) rather than location checks.

**Q4. Duplication between `encryptedRunnerClient.ts`, `crypto/noiseIk.ts`, `runtimeTransport.ts`.** The layering here is actually correct and is the best-factored part of the codebase: `noiseIk.ts` owns Noise IK framing and knows nothing about HTTP; `encryptedRunnerClient.ts` owns capability issuance, relay handshake, and RPC framing; `runtimeTransport.ts` owns path-to-scope policy. No overlapping responsibility was found. The real duplications are narrower: base64url encoding exists three times (`encryptedRunnerClient.ts:85-96`, `runtimeRef.ts:17-27`, `encryptedUpload.ts:22-26`); session-byte limits exist three times with three values (`encryptedRunnerClient.ts:15` = 64 KiB, `runtimeTransport.ts:90` = 256 KiB, `encryptedUpload.ts:10` = 128 MiB); and `encryptedUpload.ts` bypasses the `runtimeTransport` policy layer entirely (F7). The bigger duplication is cross-language: `requiredScope` versus the backend `_required_scope` (F6).

**Q5. Data-shape leakage.** Backend wire formats are used raw in components. `models/sessionModels.ts` covers only model refs and thinking levels. 98 snake_case wire-field accesses were counted across 7 UI files (F9). Validated boundary mapping exists and works well in `runner/repositories.ts`, `runtime/promptStream.ts`, and `runtime/terminalChannel.ts`, but is absent for repos, workspaces, sessions, messages, runners, provider connections, and pi config.

- `pages/Settings.tsx:62-64` `defaultOauthInstructions()` returns a 240-character user-facing paragraph from a function. That is content in a code position; it belongs with the other copy.

Data-shape leakage.** Backend wire formats are used raw in components. `models/sessionModels.ts` covers only model refs and thinking levels. 98 snake_case wire-field accesses were counted across 7 UI files (F9). Validated boundary mapping exists and works well in `runner/repositories.ts`, `runtime/promptStream.ts`, and `runtime/terminalChannel.ts`, but is absent for repos, workspaces, sessions, messages, runners, provider connections, and pi config.

2. **F13 + F8 item 4** -- delete `showMenu`, `streamPrompt`, `cancelSession`, and the fallback branches. Pure subtraction, roughly 120 lines, and it halves the branching in `useAgentStream`.

4. **F9 + F8 item 4 (resource functions)** -- add `models/*` mappers and named resource functions. This is what actually shrinks `Sidebar.tsx` and `WorkspaceInspector.tsx`.
5. **F1, F3, F4** -- split the three god components using the boundaries identified above, once 3 and 4 have removed the shared logic they currently inline.

- `runtime/promptStream.ts:67-124` and `runtime/terminalChannel.ts:46-59` validate every field of every response before use, including sequence contiguity (`promptStream.ts:110-112`, `terminalChannel.ts:181-183`). This is the correct boundary discipline.

# Frontend Software Design Review (A Philosophy of Software Design lens)

Scope: `/Users/user/projects/yinshi/frontend/src` only. `frontend/dist` and `node_modules` were excluded.

Method: full reads of the ten largest source files. Targeted greps covered all 56 non-test modules. `npx tsc --noEmit` was run and passes with no errors. No files were modified.

Note on inputs: the task referenced `plan.md` and `progress.md` at the repository root. Neither file exists. `docs/plans/` and `code_reviews/` were checked instead for context.

---

## 1. Quantitative summary

| File | Lines | `useState` | `useEffect` | Component functions | Raw `/api/...` literals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `components/Sidebar.tsx` | 1203 | 26 | 7 | 5 | 13 |
| `pages/Settings.tsx` | 968 | 24 | 4 | 5 | 4 |
| `components/CloudRunnerSection.tsx` | 837 | 17 | 2 | 2 | 4 |
| `components/WorkspaceInspector.tsx` | 757 | 12 | 4 | 4 | 7 |
| `pages/Session.tsx` | 668 | 12 | 7 | 1 | 4 |
| `api/client.ts` | 579 | -- | -- | -- | 5 |
| `runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts` | 555 | -- | -- | -- | 2 |
| `components/ChatView.tsx` | 400 | 5 | 1 | 1 | 0 |

Cross-cutting counts:

- 60 raw `/api/...` URL literals across 16 modules. 32 of them sit in `components/` and `pages/`.
- 27 references to `window.yinshiDesktop` across 9 non-test modules.
- 29 direct inspections of `RuntimeRef.location` across 9 non-test modules.
- 5 independent copies of `RESOURCE_ID_PATTERN = /^[0-9a-f]{32}$/`.
- 3 independent base64url encoders.
- 4 call sites fetching `GET /api/settings/runner`. They use 4 different usability rules.
- 3 independent `formatTimestamp` implementations.

---

## 2. Findings

### F1. Sidebar.tsx is a god module with six responsibilities (severity: high)

`components/Sidebar.tsx` holds 26 `useState` calls and 7 effects in one file. The four components are `Sidebar` (`:166-498`), `RepoSection` (`:500-806`), `WorkspaceItem` (`:808-953`), and `ImportForm` (`:955-1203`).

The distinct responsibilities are:

1. **Multi-runtime discovery and fan-out fetch.** `loadRepos` (`:188-259`) probes the hosted runtime (`:200-217`). It then probes the BYOC runner (`:218-243`). It aggregates three repository lists. It also computes a per-location error banner list (`locationErrors`, `:185`).
2. **GitHub installation state and OAuth callback handling.** See `githubNoticeFromSearch` (`:97-129`), `loadGitHubInstallations` (`:261-281`), and the URL-rewriting effect (`:283-308`).
3. **Repository-level settings editing.** `RepoSection` owns an AGENTS.md draft editor. Its state sits at `:522-525`. Its handlers sit at `:589-628`. Its 60-line textarea form sits at `:695-757`.
4. **Workspace and session lifecycle.** `createBranch` (`:546-573`) creates a workspace, creates a session, then navigates. `WorkspaceItem.openOrCreateSession` (`:845-873`) duplicates that create-then-navigate logic.
5. **Application chrome.** Theme toggle, settings navigation, logout, and an inlined gear SVG all sit at `:398-483`.
6. **Repository import validation.** `ImportForm.handleSubmit` (`:1008-1063`) classifies input as git URL, local path, or GitHub shorthand. It also enforces runtime-specific import rules.

Consequence: three unrelated concerns share one 1203-line file. A GitHub change, an AGENTS.md change, and a runtime discovery change all land here. The name `Sidebar` describes a screen region. It does not describe an information-hiding boundary.

Suggested restructuring:

- Extract `useRuntimeRepositories()` into `runtime/`. It returns `{ repos, runtimes, locationErrors, loading, error, reload }`. It becomes the single home for runtime and repo discovery. This also fixes F5.
- Extract `components/RepoSettingsForm.tsx` for the AGENTS.md editor. Move state `:522-525`, handlers `:589-628`, and markup `:695-757`.
- Extract `hooks/useGitHubInstallations.ts` for responsibility 2, including `githubNoticeFromSearch`.
- Merge `createBranch` and `openOrCreateSession` into one `startSession(transport, runtime, workspaceId)` helper. Place it next to `runtimeResourceId`.

Target: `Sidebar.tsx` under 300 lines, holding layout and composition only.

---

### F2. Runner usability is decided in four places with three different rules (severity: high, correctness risk)

The predicate is duplicated and has already diverged.

| Location | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `runtime/resolveRuntime.ts:31-38` | runner exists, id matches, `status !== "revoked"`, `noise_key_confirmed`, `noise_public_key` |
| `pages/Settings.tsx:751-755` | `noise_key_confirmed`, `noise_public_key`, `status !== "revoked"` |
| `components/Sidebar.tsx:222` | `noise_key_confirmed`, `noise_public_key`. **No status check.** |
| `components/CloudRunnerSection.tsx:358, :378, :401` | `noise_public_key`, `noise_key_confirmed`. **No status check.** |

`Sidebar.tsx:222` omits the revoked check. A revoked runner therefore still yields a `byoc` entry in `availableRuntimes` (`:225-229`). Its repositories are still listed (`:232-243`). The user can then select that runtime in `ImportForm` and attempt an import. In the same session, `Settings.tsx` would already have hidden the BYOC option.

This is textbook information leakage. One design decision lives in four modules. The copies no longer agree.

Suggested restructuring: add `runtime/runnerIdentity.ts` exporting `loadPairedRunnerRuntime(): Promise<RuntimeRef | null>`. All four call sites consume it. `resolveRuntimeRef` uses the same helper plus an id-match assertion.

---

### F3. Settings.tsx `ProviderCard` mixes three auth mechanisms and a poll loop (severity: high)

`pages/Settings.tsx:66-511` is one component with 15 `useState` calls (`:77-101`). It implements five things:

1. API key form state. See `secret`, `label`, `config`, and `missingRequiredField` (`:171-188`).
2. `api_key_with_config` secret-shape construction (`structuredSecret`, `:152-169`). This encodes a backend payload contract inside a render-time `useMemo`.
3. A full OAuth flow. `connectProvider` (`:212-250`) contains a 600-iteration polling loop at `:227-241`. Each iteration waits one second on `setTimeout`.
4. Manual OAuth callback paste handling (`submitOauthCallbackInput`, `:252-284`).
5. Connection deletion (`:286-299`).

`resetOauthFlowState` (`:103-112`) and `applyOauthFlowState` (`:114-131`) exist only to keep 7 related state values consistent. That is the signal for one state object or one reducer.

Additional risk: the loop at `:227-241` is not bound to an `AbortController` or to unmount. Only the `connecting` flag guards re-entry. After unmount, `setError` and `applyOauthFlowState` still fire. Up to 600 requests still go out.

Suggested restructuring:

- Extract `hooks/useProviderOauthFlow(transport, providerId)`. It returns `{ state, start, submitManualInput, cancel }`. Drive the poll loop with `AbortController` and clean it up in `useEffect`. Collapse the 7 OAuth state values into one object.
- Extract `models/providerConnection.ts`. Move `buildInitialConfig`, `normalizeFieldValue`, secret construction, and required-field validation. That module then owns the wire payload for `POST /api/settings/connections`.
- Split `ProviderCard` into `ApiKeyProviderForm` and `OauthProviderForm`. The `hasKeyForm` and `hasOauth` booleans at `:133-135` already mark the boundary.

---

### F4. CloudRunnerSection.tsx conflates four concerns (severity: med-high)

`components/CloudRunnerSection.tsx:250-732` holds 17 `useState` calls (`:251-273`). Seven async operations serve four different concerns:

1. Provisioning: `loadRunner` (`:275-294`), `createRunner` (`:301-335`), `revokeRunner` (`:436-451`).
2. Noise identity pairing: `confirmRunnerIdentity` (`:337-355`).
3. Connectivity diagnostics: `checkRunnerConnection` (`:357-375`).
4. BYOC repository CRUD: `loadRunnerRepositories` (`:377-398`), `importRepositoryToRunner` (`:400-434`), and `RunnerRepositoryPanel` (`:734-837`).

Concern 4 is a repository browser embedded in a settings section. It duplicates what `Sidebar.tsx:218-243` already does through `listRunnerRepositories`. Concern 3 is a single button that calls `checkEncryptedRunnerHealth`.

The static option catalogue at `:31-83` is 53 lines of copy and warnings. It is content, not logic. It is interleaved with behaviour.

`optionById` (`:172-178`) throws on an unknown id. Its only caller is `:462` with `selectedOption`. That value comes from `optionForRunner` (`:157-170`) or from a radio input restricted to `RUNNER_OPTIONS`. The throw is unreachable. No caller can handle it. Per "define errors out of existence", it should return a default or take a narrower parameter type.

Suggested restructuring: move `RUNNER_OPTIONS`, `STORAGE_LABELS`, `optionForRunner`, `optionById`, `runnerProfileValue`, and `isRunnerStorageProfile` into `runner/runnerStorageOptions.ts`. Extract `hooks/useCloudRunner()` for concerns 1 to 3. Move `RunnerRepositoryPanel` and its two handlers into their own component file. That file consumes `runner/repositories.ts` directly.

---

### F5. Runtime selection is decided in at least six places (severity: high)

The intended single decision point is `runtime/useRuntimeResource.ts:29-79`. It parses the encoded id, resolves the ref, and builds the transport. `pages/Session.tsx:65-69` uses it correctly. That is the model to follow.

Every other consumer re-derives the answer.

| Location | Independent decision |
| --- | --- |
| `components/Sidebar.tsx:172-174` | builds `defaultRuntime` from `window.yinshiDesktop` |
| `components/Sidebar.tsx:200-217` | decides that hosted probing is desktop-only |
| `components/Sidebar.tsx:269` | picks hosted or default for GitHub installs |
| `pages/Settings.tsx:604-606` | rebuilds `primaryRuntime` inside `RuntimeLocationSelector` |
| `pages/Settings.tsx:696-698` | rebuilds `primaryRuntime` again in `Settings` |
| `api/client.ts:376, :408` | decides desktop-hosted routing by path membership |
| `runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:266, :331` | decides `hostedApi` against `api`, and hosted upload routing |

`runtime/runtimeRef.ts:64-68` already exports `defaultRuntimeRef({ desktop })`. That is the correct home for the decision. Only `parseRuntimeResourceId` uses it today. Three sites reimplement it inline: `Sidebar.tsx:172`, `Settings.tsx:604`, and `Settings.tsx:697`.

Suggested restructuring:

- Replace the three inline ternaries with `defaultRuntimeRef`. Add `runtime/environment.ts` exporting `isDesktop()`. That cuts 27 `window.yinshiDesktop` references down to about 8 genuine bridge call sites.
- Add `runtime/useAvailableRuntimes()` as the sole producer of the runtime list. `Sidebar` and `Settings` consume it. This also fixes F2.

---

### F6. The BYOC scope table is duplicated across frontend and backend (severity: med)

`runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:96-206` (`requiredScope`) is a near line-for-line port of `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:131-215` (`_required_scope`). The same 18 path regexes appear in both. See `runtimeTransport.ts:48-89` against the module-level patterns in `runner_rpc.py`.

Defence in depth justifies a client-side scope request. The copies have already diverged. The backend handles four pi-upload path patterns at `runner_rpc.py:206-215`. The frontend table has no upload entries at all. It would throw `"BYOC runtime method or path is not allowed"` for them. The upload flow therefore bypasses `createRuntimeTransport` entirely. See F7.

Adding one BYOC-reachable route now needs coordinated edits in two languages. No test asserts that the two tables agree.

Suggested restructuring: generate both tables from one declarative route-scope manifest checked into the repository. A cheaper alternative is a contract test that enumerates the frontend table and asserts each entry against the backend table.

---

### F7. `encryptedUpload` bypasses the transport policy layer (severity: med)

`runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:322-341` special-cases `upload`. For `byoc` it calls `uploadEncryptedPiConfig`. For desktop-hosted it calls `uploadHostedPiConfig`. Both open their own connections.

`runtime/encryptedUpload.ts:150-186` calls `connectEncryptedRunner` directly. It hard-codes `scopes: ["pi.configure"]` at `:159`. It skips `requiredScope`, `parseByocPath`, and `validateRuntime`.

The result is two independent BYOC request paths with three different session limits:

- `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:15` defaults to 64 KiB.
- `runtimeTransport.ts:90` uses 256 KiB.
- `encryptedUpload.ts:10` uses 128 MiB.

`runtimeTransport.ts:323-338` also hard-codes one allowed upload path, `"/api/settings/pi-config/upload"`. `encryptedUpload.ts:99-131` never sends that path. It sends `/api/settings/pi-config/uploads`, then `/uploads/{id}/chunks/{i}`, then `/uploads/{id}/complete`. The guard validates a path that is then discarded.

Suggested restructuring: give `RuntimeTransport` an explicit `uploadPiConfig(file)` method instead of a generic `upload(path, file)`. The path then stops being a caller concern. Move the session-byte constants into one `runtime/limits.ts`.

---

### F8. `api/client.ts` is over-general and over-layered, not shallow (severity: med)

Direct answer: `api/client.ts` is **not** a one-function-per-endpoint wrapper. It exposes 6 generic verb methods on `api` (`:414-440`), 6 more on `hostedApi` (`:442-451`), plus `streamPrompt` (`:515-572`) and `cancelSession` (`:574-579`).

The 579 lines break down roughly as follows. Wire type declarations occupy `:1-254`, which is 25 exported interfaces. Error normalisation occupies `:256-320`. Transport occupies `:322-451`. SSE handling occupies `:453-579`.

The abstraction value is real but thin. The module centralises credentials, the CSRF header, the 401 redirect, error normalisation, and 204 handling. `_readApiError` and `_normalizeErrorPayload` (`:256-320`) are genuinely deep.

The problems are the opposite of shallowness:

1. **Pass-through layering.** The same 6-method signature is declared four times. See `JsonApiClient` (`runtimeTransport.ts:22-29`), `RuntimeTransport` (`runtimeTransport.ts:36-44`), `api` (`client.ts:414-440`), and `hostedApi` (`client.ts:442-451`). `hostedApi.upload` at `:450` is a literal pass-through to `api.upload`. `hostedRequest` (`:403-411`) delegates with an unchanged signature.
2. **Overexposure of the URL space.** The interface is `get<T>(path)`. Every caller must know URL structure. 32 raw `/api/...` literals sit in components and pages. `Sidebar.tsx` alone holds 13.
3. **Nonobvious desktop routing.** `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` (`:317-321`) silently re-routes exactly three paths through the desktop bridge. A reader of `api.get("/api/settings/runner")` at `Sidebar.tsx:220` cannot see this. `request` (`:374-380`) also performs the check twice, once directly and once inside `desktopHostedRequest`. That is a conjoined-method smell.
4. **Dead legacy streaming path.** `streamPrompt` and `cancelSession` are used only at `useAgentStream.ts:127` and `:193`. Those branches run when `runtimeTransport` is falsy. In `pages/Session.tsx:66-70`, `id` and `transport` both derive from the same `runtimeResource` object. They are undefined together. `sendPrompt` then returns early at `useAgentStream.ts:47`. The SSE branch is unreachable. That is about 90 dead lines plus a branch that doubles the cost of reading the hook.

Suggested restructuring:

- Delete `streamPrompt`, `cancelSession`, and the fallback branches at `useAgentStream.ts:120-134` and `:186-195`.
- Collapse `hostedApi` into `api`. Alternatively move `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` into `runtimeTransport.ts`, beside the other routing decisions.
- Move the 254 lines of wire types into `api/wireTypes.ts`. `client.ts` then reads as transport only.
- Add named resource functions such as `fetchRepos(transport)` and `patchWorkspaceState(...)`. Components then stop carrying URL literals. This is the highest-leverage change for shrinking `Sidebar.tsx` and `WorkspaceInspector.tsx`.

---

### F9. Backend wire shapes are used raw in components (severity: med)

`models/sessionModels.ts` maps only model refs and thinking levels. It is 169 lines and 9 exported functions. Everything else flows raw into the UI.

Snake_case wire-field accesses in presentation code, counted per file:

| File | Snake_case field accesses |
| --- | --- |
| `pages/Settings.tsx` | 24 |
| `components/PiReleaseNotesSection.tsx` | 19 |
| `components/Sidebar.tsx` | 17 |
| `components/CloudRunnerSection.tsx` | 16 |
| `components/PiConfigSection.tsx` | 10 |
| `components/ToolCallBlock.tsx` | 8 |
| `pages/Session.tsx` | 4 |

Concrete instances:

- `Sidebar.tsx:222-243` reads `noise_key_confirmed`, `noise_public_key`, and `id`. It then hand-builds a `RuntimeRef`. `Settings.tsx:751-760` repeats this. See F2.
- `Sidebar.tsx:522`, `:592-596`, and `:601` read and write `repo.agents_md`. Line `:593` encodes a backend null convention inside a JSX component.
- `CloudRunnerSection.tsx:137-144` reaches into `runner.capabilities[key]`. That field is an untyped `Record<string, unknown>` from `client.ts:87`. The component defends against non-string values inline at `:142`.
- `Session.tsx:116-135` maps `Message` rows to `ChatMessage` inline inside `loadHistory`. Line `:129` performs an unchecked `m.role` cast.
- `WorkspaceInspector.tsx:246-249` decodes a `{ content?, diff? }` union by branching on `mode`. The component therefore knows that two endpoints name their payload field differently.

The correct pattern already exists elsewhere. `runner/repositories.ts:9-24`, `runtime/promptStream.ts:67-124`, and `runtime/terminalChannel.ts:46-59` all validate and map at the boundary. That discipline is simply absent for settings, runners, repos, and messages.

Suggested restructuring: add `models/runnerModels.ts`, `models/repoModels.ts`, and `models/messageModels.ts`. Move the `Message` to `ChatMessage` mapping out of `Session.tsx:116-135`. Components should never touch a snake_case field.

---

### F10. Repetition of small utilities (severity: low-med, broad)

| Duplicated element | Locations |
| --- | --- |
| `RESOURCE_ID_PATTERN` | `encryptedUpload.ts:12`, `terminalChannel.ts:3`, `runtimeRef.ts:3`, `promptStream.ts:8`, plus `RESOURCE_ID` at `runtimeTransport.ts:48` |
| base64url encoding | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:85-96`, `runtimeRef.ts:17-27`, `encryptedUpload.ts:22-26` |
| `formatTimestamp` | `Settings.tsx:22-27`, `CloudRunnerSection.tsx:113-118`, `PiConfigSection.tsx:22-27`. Bodies are identical. Fallback strings differ. |
| Error-message extraction | `CloudRunnerSection.tsx:133-135`, `usePiConfig.ts:31-36`, plus 18 inline ternaries across `WorkspaceInspector.tsx:257,283`, `useCatalog.ts:29`, `usePiReleaseNotes.ts:26`, `useRuntimeResource.ts:71`, and 5 sites in `Settings.tsx` |
| Pointer-drag resize | `Session.tsx:478-500` and `WorkspaceInspector.tsx:624-648` are structurally identical. Their readers `Session.tsx:56-63` and `WorkspaceInspector.tsx:77-84` differ only in storage key and bounds. |
| Runtime identity string | `Sidebar.tsx:45-50`, `piCommandsCache.ts:20-23`, `runtimeRef.ts:70-85`. Three encodings of the same idea, in three formats. |

`pages/Session.tsx:65-88` declares 12 state values in one component. Three concerns are separable:

1. **Slash-command interpreter.** `handleCommand` (`:258-343`) is an 85-line switch over five commands. It inlines a blob-download implementation at `:314-330`.
2. **Model resolution and mutation.** `updateSessionModel` (`:190-256`) validates provider connections, resolves the model, sends a PATCH, and announces the result. 3. **Catalogue sorting for a select element.** The 45-line `useMemo` at `:345-391` sorts models by connection, then provider label, then model label. This is model-domain logic in a page.

The builtin command list is stated three times. See `ChatView.tsx:34-40`, the `/help` text at `Session.tsx:266-274`, and the switch arms at `Session.tsx:276-342`. These can drift apart.

Move `handleCommand` into `session/slashCommands.ts` as one registry of `{ name, description, run }`. `ChatView` and `Session` then share one list. Split `updateSessionModel` into a pure mutation plus caller-side announcement.

---

### F12. `useAgentStream` conjoins queueing, cancellation, and two transports (severity: med)

See `hooks/useAgentStream.ts:35-215`. Three functions cannot be read independently. `sendPrompt` (`:200-222`) writes `queuedPromptRef` and then calls `cancel` (`:180-198`). The `finally` block of `startPrompt` (`:161-177`) then re-invokes `startPrompt` for the queued prompt. Understanding one function requires reading the other two. That is the conjoined-methods flag.

The recursive re-entry at `:172-176` is also nonobvious. `startPrompt` calls itself from its own `finally` block. There is no depth bound. Repeated steering builds an implicit chain.

`upsertTurn` and `scheduleUpsert` (`:70-108`) implement rAF-batched message coalescing in the same closure. That is a separate, testable concern.

Suggested restructuring: model the run lifecycle as an explicit reducer over `idle | running | stopping`. That enum already exists at `:33`. Hold the queued prompt in that state, not in a ref read from a `finally` block. Extract the rAF batching into `utils/turnBuffer.ts`.

- `components/ChatView.tsx:78` declares `showMenu`. It is written at `:146`, `:197`, `:208`, and `:238`. It is **never read**. `menuVisible` (`:141`) is derived from `slashFilter` and `filteredCommands`. Delete the state and its four setters.
- `components/ChatView.tsx:211` lists `streaming` as a `handleSubmit` dependency. The body at `:180-210` never references it.
- `api/client.ts:515-579` and the branches at `useAgentStream.ts:120-134` and `:186-195` are unreachable. See F8 item 4.
- `runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:324-327` validates an upload path that is never requested. See F7.

---

### F14. Comment and naming observations (severity: low)

Positive examples: `api/piCommandsCache.ts:6-8` and `:31-34`, `ChatView.tsx:8-11`, `:123-131`, `:159-162`, and `Session.tsx:411-413`. These record why, not what. They preserve information the code cannot express.

Problems:

- `Session.tsx:112` restates the function name below it.
- `Sidebar.tsx:552` restates the next four lines.
- `Settings.tsx:62-64` returns a 240-character user-facing paragraph from a function. That is content in a code position.
- `LocatedRepo` (`Sidebar.tsx:29-32`) pairs a repo with its runtime. `RepoWithRuntime` reads better.
- `locationErrors` (`:185`) holds sentences, not errors. `unavailableRuntimeMessages` matches its content.
- `data` at `Sidebar.tsx:191` and `:273` is broad. So are `runtimeState` and `runtimeResource` at `Session.tsx:66-67`.
- `runnerHealth` (`CloudRunnerSection.tsx:263`) is `string | null` and holds a success sentence. `healthMessage` is accurate.
- `runnerStatusClass` (`CloudRunnerSection.tsx:120`) takes `string`, then casts to `CloudRunnerStatus` at `:122`. A narrower parameter type removes both the cast and the fallback.

## 3. Direct answers to the five questions

**Q1. God components.** Confirmed for all three. `Sidebar.tsx` holds 6 responsibilities and 26 `useState` calls (F1). `Settings.tsx` holds 5 top-level responsibilities: account display, desktop profile management, FileVault status, runtime-location selection, and tab routing. It also contains the `ProviderCard` sub-god with 15 `useState` calls (F3). `CloudRunnerSection.tsx` holds 4 concerns and 17 `useState` calls (F4).

**Q2. Is `api/client.ts` deep or shallow?** Neither, precisely. It exposes 14 public members plus 25 wire interfaces. It is not a per-endpoint wrapper. Its centralised credential, CSRF, 401, and error handling is genuine depth. Four separate failures undercut that. The 6-verb signature is redeclared four times across two files. The URL space is fully exposed, with 32 literals in UI code. A hidden path-membership rule re-routes three paths (`:317-321`). About 90 lines of SSE code are unreachable. See F8.

**Q3. Does `runtime/` leak transport details?** Yes, although the abstraction itself is sound. `RuntimeTransport` (`runtimeTransport.ts:36-44`) is the right interface. `useRuntimeResource` is the right entry point, and `Session.tsx` proves it works. However, the runtime choice is made in at least 6 places (F5). `RuntimeRef.location` is inspected 29 times across 9 modules. Some of those inspections are presentation code that should not care. `WorkspaceInspector.tsx:321` hides the download link for `byoc`. `Sidebar.tsx:516` collapses BYOC repos by default. `promptStream.ts:174` picks a poll delay by location. `piCommandsCache.ts:22` keys its cache by location. The first two are UI policy driven by a transport detail. They should read a capability flag on the transport instead.

**Q4. Duplication across `encryptedRunnerClient.ts`, `crypto/noiseIk.ts`, and `runtimeTransport.ts`.** The layering here is correct and is the best-factored part of the codebase. `noiseIk.ts` owns Noise IK framing and knows nothing about HTTP. `encryptedRunnerClient.ts` owns capability issuance, relay handshake, and RPC framing. `runtimeTransport.ts` owns path-to-scope policy. No overlapping responsibility was found. The real duplications are narrower. Base64url encoding exists three times. Session-byte limits exist three times with three values (F7). `encryptedUpload.ts` bypasses the policy layer entirely (F7). The larger duplication is cross-language, between `requiredScope` and the backend `_required_scope` (F6).

**Q5. Data-shape leakage.** Backend wire formats are used raw in components. `models/sessionModels.ts` covers only model refs and thinking levels. 98 snake_case wire-field accesses were counted across 7 UI files (F9). Validated boundary mapping works well in `runner/repositories.ts`, `runtime/promptStream.ts`, and `runtime/terminalChannel.ts`. It is absent for repos, workspaces, sessions, messages, runners, provider connections, and pi config.

## 4. Suggested remediation order

1. **F2.** Unify the runner usability predicate. Smallest change. It removes a real behavioural inconsistency at `Sidebar.tsx:222`.
2. **F13 and F8 item 4.** Delete `showMenu`, `streamPrompt`, `cancelSession`, and the dead branches. Pure subtraction of about 120 lines. It halves the branching in `useAgentStream`.
3. **F5.** Add `runtime/environment.ts`. Route all default-runtime construction through `defaultRuntimeRef`. Then add `useAvailableRuntimes()`.
4. **F9 and F8 resource functions.** Add `models/*` mappers and named resource functions. This is what actually shrinks `Sidebar.tsx` and `WorkspaceInspector.tsx`.
5. **F1, F3, F4.** Split the three god components along the boundaries above. Do this after steps 3 and 4 remove the shared logic they inline today.
6. **F10.** Consolidate the small utilities as the earlier extractions touch them.
7. **F6 and F7.** Unify the scope table source and the encrypted upload path. Highest coordination cost. Lowest urgency. The divergence is already visible.

- `runtime/promptStream.ts:67-124` and `runtime/terminalChannel.ts:46-59` validate every response field before use. Both also check sequence contiguity, at `promptStream.ts:110-112` and `terminalChannel.ts:181-183`.

- `api/piCommandsCache.ts` is small and well commented. It has a clear invalidation contract and per-runtime keying.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` passes cleanly. 20 test files cover hooks, runtime modules, crypto, and the larger components.

# Frontend Software Design Review

A Philosophy of Software Design lens applied to `/Users/user/projects/yinshi/frontend/src`. The directories `frontend/dist` plus `node_modules` were excluded.

Method: full reads of the ten largest source files. Targeted greps covered all 56 non-test modules. `npx tsc --noEmit` was run and passes with no errors. No files were modified.

The task referenced `plan.md` plus `progress.md` at the repository root. Neither file exists. `docs/plans/` and `code_reviews/` were read instead for context.

## 1. Quantitative summary

| File | Lines | `useState` | `useEffect` | Components | Raw `/api/...` literals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `components/Sidebar.tsx` | 1203 | 26 | 7 | 5 | 13 |
| `pages/Settings.tsx` | 968 | 24 | 4 | 5 | 4 |
| `components/CloudRunnerSection.tsx` | 837 | 17 | 2 | 2 | 4 |
| `components/WorkspaceInspector.tsx` | 757 | 12 | 4 | 4 | 7 |
| `pages/Session.tsx` | 668 | 12 | 7 | 1 | 4 |
| `api/client.ts` | 579 | -- | -- | -- | 5 |
| `runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts` | 555 | -- | -- | -- | 2 |
| `components/ChatView.tsx` | 400 | 5 | 1 | 1 | 0 |

Cross-cutting counts follow. The codebase carries 60 raw `/api/...` URL literals across 16 modules, of which 32 sit inside `components/` or `pages/`. The global `window.yinshiDesktop` is referenced 27 times across 9 non-test modules. The discriminant `RuntimeRef.location` is inspected 29 times across 9 non-test modules. Five modules each declare a private `RESOURCE_ID_PATTERN = /^[0-9a-f]{32}$/`. Three modules each implement base64url encoding. Four call sites fetch `GET /api/settings/runner` under four different usability rules. Three files each define their own `formatTimestamp`.

## 2. Findings

### F1. Sidebar.tsx is a god module carrying six responsibilities (severity: high)

`components/Sidebar.tsx` holds 26 `useState` calls plus 7 effects in one file. Its four components are `Sidebar` (`:166-498`), `RepoSection` (`:500-806`), `WorkspaceItem` (`:808-953`), and `ImportForm` (`:955-1203`).

The first responsibility is multi-runtime discovery with a fan-out fetch. `loadRepos` (`:188-259`) probes the hosted runtime at `:200-217`, then probes the BYOC runner at `:218-243`, then aggregates three repository lists. It also computes a per-location banner list held in `locationErrors` (`:185`).

The second responsibility is GitHub installation state plus OAuth callback handling. See `githubNoticeFromSearch` (`:97-129`), `loadGitHubInstallations` (`:261-281`), plus the URL-rewriting effect (`:283-308`).

The third responsibility is repository-level settings editing. `RepoSection` owns an AGENTS.md draft editor whose state sits at `:522-525`, whose handlers sit at `:589-628`, and whose 60-line textarea form sits at `:695-757`.

The fourth responsibility is workspace plus session lifecycle. `createBranch` (`:546-573`) creates a workspace, creates a session, then routes the user to it. `WorkspaceItem.openOrCreateSession` (`:845-873`) duplicates that create-then-route logic.

The fifth responsibility is application chrome. The theme toggle, the settings link, the logout button, plus an inlined gear SVG all sit at `:398-483`.

The sixth responsibility is repository import validation. `ImportForm.handleSubmit` (`:1008-1063`) classifies user input as a git URL, a local path, or GitHub shorthand. It then enforces runtime-specific import rules.

The consequence is that unrelated concerns share one 1203-line file. A GitHub change, an AGENTS.md change, or a runtime discovery change all land here. The name `Sidebar` describes a screen region rather than an information-hiding boundary.

Suggested restructuring. Extract `useRuntimeRepositories()` into `runtime/`, returning `{ repos, runtimes, locationErrors, loading, error, reload }`. That hook becomes the single home for runtime plus repo discovery, which also fixes F5. Extract `components/RepoSettingsForm.tsx` for the AGENTS.md editor by moving state `:522-525`, handlers `:589-628`, plus markup `:695-757`. Extract `hooks/useGitHubInstallations.ts` for the second responsibility, including `githubNoticeFromSearch`. Merge `createBranch` with `openOrCreateSession` into one `startSession(transport, runtime, workspaceId)` helper placed beside `runtimeResourceId`. The target is a `Sidebar.tsx` under 300 lines holding layout plus composition only.

### F2. Runner usability is decided in four places under three rules (severity: high, correctness risk)

The predicate is duplicated and has already diverged.

| Location | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `runtime/resolveRuntime.ts:31-38` | runner exists, id matches, status is not revoked, key confirmed, key present |
| `pages/Settings.tsx:751-755` | key confirmed, key present, status is not revoked |
| `components/Sidebar.tsx:222` | key confirmed, key present. No status check. |
| `components/CloudRunnerSection.tsx:358, :378, :401` | key present, key confirmed. No status check. |

`Sidebar.tsx:222` omits the revoked check. A revoked runner therefore still yields a `byoc` entry in `availableRuntimes` (`:225-229`), and its repositories are still listed (`:232-243`). The user can then select that runtime inside `ImportForm` and attempt an import. During the same session, `Settings.tsx` would already have hidden the BYOC option.

This is information leakage in the classic sense. One design decision lives in four modules, and the copies no longer agree.

Suggested restructuring. Add `runtime/runnerIdentity.ts` exporting `loadPairedRunnerRuntime(): Promise<RuntimeRef | null>`. All four call sites consume it. `resolveRuntimeRef` uses the same helper plus an id-match assertion.

### F3. Settings.tsx ProviderCard mixes three auth mechanisms with a poll loop (severity: high)

`pages/Settings.tsx:66-511` is one component holding 15 `useState` calls (`:77-101`). It implements API key form state through `secret`, `label`, `config`, plus `missingRequiredField` (`:171-188`). It implements `api_key_with_config` secret-shape construction in `structuredSecret` (`:152-169`), which encodes a backend payload contract inside a render-time `useMemo`. It implements a full OAuth flow in `connectProvider` (`:212-250`), whose 600-iteration polling loop at `:227-241` waits one second per iteration. It implements manual OAuth callback paste handling in `submitOauthCallbackInput` (`:252-284`). It also implements connection deletion at `:286-299`.

`resetOauthFlowState` (`:103-112`) plus `applyOauthFlowState` (`:114-131`) exist only to keep 7 related state values consistent. That is the signal for one state object or one reducer.

There is an additional runtime risk. The loop at `:227-241` is not bound to an `AbortController` or to unmount. Only the `connecting` flag guards re-entry. After unmount, `setError` plus `applyOauthFlowState` still fire, and up to 600 requests still go out.

Suggested restructuring. Extract `hooks/useProviderOauthFlow(transport, providerId)` returning `{ state, start, submitManualInput, cancel }`, driving the poll loop with an `AbortController` cleaned up in `useEffect`. Collapse the 7 OAuth state values into one object. Extract `models/providerConnection.ts` to hold `buildInitialConfig`, `normalizeFieldValue`, secret construction, plus required-field validation. That module then owns the wire payload for `POST /api/settings/connections`. Split `ProviderCard` into `ApiKeyProviderForm` plus `OauthProviderForm`, since the `hasKeyForm` and `hasOauth` booleans at `:133-135` already mark the boundary.

### F4. CloudRunnerSection.tsx conflates four concerns (severity: med-high)

`components/CloudRunnerSection.tsx:250-732` holds 17 `useState` calls (`:251-273`). Seven async operations serve four different concerns. Provisioning covers `loadRunner` (`:275-294`), `createRunner` (`:301-335`), plus `revokeRunner` (`:436-451`). Noise identity pairing covers `confirmRunnerIdentity` (`:337-355`). Connectivity diagnostics covers `checkRunnerConnection` (`:357-375`). BYOC repository CRUD covers `loadRunnerRepositories` (`:377-398`), `importRepositoryToRunner` (`:400-434`), plus `RunnerRepositoryPanel` (`:734-837`).

The fourth concern is a repository browser embedded inside a settings section. It duplicates what `Sidebar.tsx:218-243` already does through `listRunnerRepositories`. The third concern is a single button that calls `checkEncryptedRunnerHealth`.

The static option catalogue at `:31-83` is 53 lines of copy plus warnings. It is display content interleaved with behaviour, and it belongs in its own module.

`optionById` (`:172-178`) throws on an unknown id. Its only caller is `:462` passing `selectedOption`. That value comes from `optionForRunner` (`:157-170`) or from a radio input restricted to `RUNNER_OPTIONS`. The throw is therefore unreachable, and no caller can handle it. Following "define errors out of existence", it should return a default or accept a narrower parameter type.

Suggested restructuring. Move `RUNNER_OPTIONS`, `STORAGE_LABELS`, `optionForRunner`, `optionById`, `runnerProfileValue`, plus `isRunnerStorageProfile` into `runner/runnerStorageOptions.ts`. Extract `hooks/useCloudRunner()` for the first three concerns. Move `RunnerRepositoryPanel` with its two handlers into a component file that consumes `runner/repositories.ts` directly.

### F5. Runtime selection is decided in at least six places (severity: high)

The intended single decision point is `runtime/useRuntimeResource.ts:29-79`. It parses the encoded id, resolves the ref, then builds the transport. `pages/Session.tsx:65-69` uses it correctly and is the model to follow.

Every other consumer re-derives the answer.

| Location | Independent decision |
| --- | --- |
| `components/Sidebar.tsx:172-174` | builds `defaultRuntime` from `window.yinshiDesktop` |
| `components/Sidebar.tsx:200-217` | decides that hosted probing is desktop-only |
| `components/Sidebar.tsx:269` | picks hosted or default for GitHub installs |
| `pages/Settings.tsx:604-606` | rebuilds `primaryRuntime` inside `RuntimeLocationSelector` |
| `pages/Settings.tsx:696-698` | rebuilds `primaryRuntime` again inside `Settings` |
| `api/client.ts:376, :408` | decides desktop-hosted routing by path membership |
| `runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:266, :331` | decides `hostedApi` against `api`, plus hosted upload routing |

`runtime/runtimeRef.ts:64-68` already exports `defaultRuntimeRef({ desktop })`, which is the correct home for that decision. Only `parseRuntimeResourceId` uses it today. Three sites reimplement it inline at `Sidebar.tsx:172`, `Settings.tsx:604`, plus `Settings.tsx:697`.

Suggested restructuring. Replace the three inline ternaries with `defaultRuntimeRef`, then add `runtime/environment.ts` exporting `isDesktop()`. That cuts 27 `window.yinshiDesktop` references down to roughly 8 genuine bridge call sites. Add `runtime/useAvailableRuntimes()` as the sole producer of the runtime list, consumed by both `Sidebar` and `Settings`. That change also fixes F2.

### F6. The BYOC scope table is duplicated across frontend and backend (severity: med)

`runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:96-206` holds `requiredScope`, which is a near line-for-line port of `_required_scope` at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:131-215`. The same 18 path regexes appear on both sides. Compare `runtimeTransport.ts:48-89` against the module-level patterns in `runner_rpc.py`.

Defence in depth justifies a client-side scope request. The two copies have already diverged. The backend handles four pi-upload path patterns at `runner_rpc.py:206-215`. The frontend table has no upload entries at all, so it would throw `"BYOC runtime method or path is not allowed"` for them. The upload flow therefore bypasses `createRuntimeTransport` entirely, as described in F7.

Adding one BYOC-reachable route now requires coordinated edits in two languages. No test asserts that the two tables agree.

Suggested restructuring. Generate both tables from one declarative route-scope manifest checked into the repository. A cheaper option is a contract test that enumerates the frontend table then asserts each entry against the backend table.

### F7. encryptedUpload bypasses the transport policy layer (severity: med)

`runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:322-341` special-cases `upload`. For `byoc` it calls `uploadEncryptedPiConfig`. For desktop-hosted it calls `uploadHostedPiConfig`. Both open their own connections.

`runtime/encryptedUpload.ts:150-186` calls `connectEncryptedRunner` directly, hard-coding `scopes: ["pi.configure"]` at `:159`. It skips `requiredScope`. It also skips `parseByocPath` plus `validateRuntime`.

The result is two independent BYOC request paths under three different session limits. `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:15` defaults to 64 KiB. `runtimeTransport.ts:90` uses 256 KiB. `encryptedUpload.ts:10` uses 128 MiB.

`runtimeTransport.ts:323-338` also hard-codes one allowed upload path, `"/api/settings/pi-config/upload"`. `encryptedUpload.ts:99-131` never sends that path. It sends `/api/settings/pi-config/uploads`, then `/uploads/{id}/chunks/{i}`, then `/uploads/{id}/complete`. The guard validates a path that is discarded immediately afterwards.

Suggested restructuring. Give `RuntimeTransport` an explicit `uploadPiConfig(file)` method in place of the generic `upload(path, file)`, so the path stops being a caller concern. Move the session-byte constants into one `runtime/limits.ts`.

### F8. api/client.ts is over-general and over-layered rather than shallow (severity: med)

`api/client.ts` is no one-function-per-endpoint wrapper. It exposes 6 generic verb methods on `api` (`:414-440`), 6 more on `hostedApi` (`:442-451`), plus `streamPrompt` (`:515-572`) with `cancelSession` (`:574-579`).

The 579 lines break down as follows. Wire type declarations occupy `:1-254`, covering 25 exported interfaces. Error normalisation occupies `:256-320`. Transport occupies `:322-451`. SSE handling occupies `:453-579`.

The abstraction value is real yet thin. The module centralises credentials, the CSRF header, the 401 redirect, error normalisation, plus 204 handling. `_readApiError` with `_normalizeErrorPayload` (`:256-320`) is genuinely deep work behind a simple interface.

Four problems remain, and each is the opposite of shallowness.

Pass-through layering. The same 6-method signature is declared four times: `JsonApiClient` (`runtimeTransport.ts:22-29`), `RuntimeTransport` (`runtimeTransport.ts:36-44`), `api` (`client.ts:414-440`), plus `hostedApi` (`client.ts:442-451`). `hostedApi.upload` at `:450` is a literal pass-through to `api.upload`. `hostedRequest` (`:403-411`) delegates with an unchanged signature.

Overexposure of the URL space. The interface is `get<T>(path)`, so every caller must know URL structure. 32 raw `/api/...` literals sit inside components or pages, and `Sidebar.tsx` alone holds 13.

Nonobvious desktop routing. `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` (`:317-321`) silently re-routes exactly three paths through the desktop bridge. A reader of `api.get("/api/settings/runner")` at `Sidebar.tsx:220` cannot see that. `request` (`:374-380`) also performs the check twice, once directly and once inside `desktopHostedRequest`, which is a conjoined-method smell.

Dead legacy streaming path. `streamPrompt` plus `cancelSession` are used only at `useAgentStream.ts:127` and `:193`. Those branches run when `runtimeTransport` is falsy. In `pages/Session.tsx:66-70`, `id` plus `transport` both derive from the same `runtimeResource` object, so they are undefined together. `sendPrompt` then returns early at `useAgentStream.ts:47`. The SSE branch is unreachable. That is roughly 90 dead lines, plus a branch that doubles the cost of reading the hook.

Suggested restructuring. Delete `streamPrompt`, `cancelSession`, plus the fallback branches at `useAgentStream.ts:120-134` and `:186-195`. Collapse `hostedApi` into `api`, or move `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` into `runtimeTransport.ts` beside the other routing decisions. Move the 254 lines of wire types into `api/wireTypes.ts` so `client.ts` reads as transport only. Add named resource functions such as `fetchRepos(transport)` plus `patchWorkspaceState(...)` so components stop carrying URL literals. That last change does the most to shrink `Sidebar.tsx` with `WorkspaceInspector.tsx`.

### F9. Backend wire shapes are used raw in components (severity: med)

`models/sessionModels.ts` maps only model refs plus thinking levels, across 169 lines and 9 exported functions. Everything else flows raw into the UI.

Snake_case wire-field accesses in presentation code, counted per file:

| File | Snake_case field accesses |
| --- | --- |
| `pages/Settings.tsx` | 24 |
| `components/PiReleaseNotesSection.tsx` | 19 |
| `components/Sidebar.tsx` | 17 |
| `components/CloudRunnerSection.tsx` | 16 |
| `components/PiConfigSection.tsx` | 10 |
| `components/ToolCallBlock.tsx` | 8 |
| `pages/Session.tsx` | 4 |

Concrete instances follow. `Sidebar.tsx:222-243` reads `noise_key_confirmed`, `noise_public_key`, plus `id`, then hand-builds a `RuntimeRef`. `Settings.tsx:751-760` repeats that construction, as covered in F2. `Sidebar.tsx:522`, `:592-596`, plus `:601` read and write `repo.agents_md`, and line `:593` encodes a backend null convention inside a JSX component. `CloudRunnerSection.tsx:137-144` reaches into `runner.capabilities[key]`, an untyped `Record<string, unknown>` from `client.ts:87`, then defends against non-string values inline at `:142`. `Session.tsx:116-135` maps `Message` rows into `ChatMessage` inline inside `loadHistory`, and line `:129` performs an unchecked `m.role` cast. `WorkspaceInspector.tsx:246-249` decodes a `{ content?, diff? }` union by branching on `mode`, so the component knows that two endpoints name their payload field differently.

The correct pattern already exists elsewhere. `runner/repositories.ts:9-24`, `runtime/promptStream.ts:67-124`, plus `runtime/terminalChannel.ts:46-59` all validate then map at the boundary. That discipline is simply absent for settings, runners, repos, and message history.

Suggested restructuring. Add `models/runnerModels.ts`, `models/repoModels.ts`, plus `models/messageModels.ts`. Move the `Message` to `ChatMessage` mapping out of `Session.tsx:116-135`. No component should touch a snake_case field.

### F10. Repetition of small utilities (severity: low-med, broad)

| Duplicated element | Locations |
| --- | --- |
| `RESOURCE_ID_PATTERN` | `encryptedUpload.ts:12`, `terminalChannel.ts:3`, `runtimeRef.ts:3`, `promptStream.ts:8`, plus `RESOURCE_ID` at `runtimeTransport.ts:48` |
| base64url encoding | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:85-96`, `runtimeRef.ts:17-27`, `encryptedUpload.ts:22-26` |
| `formatTimestamp` | `Settings.tsx:22-27`, `CloudRunnerSection.tsx:113-118`, `PiConfigSection.tsx:22-27`. Bodies identical. Fallback strings differ. |
| Error-message extraction | `CloudRunnerSection.tsx:133-135`, `usePiConfig.ts:31-36`, plus 18 inline ternaries at `WorkspaceInspector.tsx:257,283`, `useCatalog.ts:29`, `usePiReleaseNotes.ts:26`, `useRuntimeResource.ts:71`, with 5 more sites in `Settings.tsx` |
| Pointer-drag resize | `Session.tsx:478-500` matches `WorkspaceInspector.tsx:624-648` structurally. Their readers `Session.tsx:56-63` and `WorkspaceInspector.tsx:77-84` differ only in storage key plus bounds. |
| Runtime identity string | `Sidebar.tsx:45-50`, `piCommandsCache.ts:20-23`, `runtimeRef.ts:70-85`. Three encodings of one idea, in three formats. |

Suggested restructuring. Create `utils/errors.ts`, `utils/format.ts`, `utils/base64url.ts`, plus `runtime/resourceId.ts`. Add `hooks/useDragSize({ storageKey, min, max, initial, axis })`. Export one `runtimeKey(runtime)` from `runtime/runtimeRef.ts`, then delete the copies.

### F11. Session.tsx mixes command dispatch with catalogue sorting and layout (severity: med)

`pages/Session.tsx:65-88` declares 12 state values in one component. Three concerns are separable.

The slash-command interpreter is `handleCommand` (`:258-343`), an 85-line switch over five commands. It inlines a blob-download implementation at `:314-330`.

Model resolution plus mutation is `updateSessionModel` (`:190-256`). It validates provider connections, resolves the model, sends a PATCH, then announces the result. The `announce: boolean` flag shows that two callers want different behaviour. `handleCommand` (`:280`) wants messages. `handleModelChange` (`:394-407`) does not, then adds its own message at `:403`.

Catalogue sorting for a select element is the 45-line `useMemo` at `:345-391`. It sorts models by connection status, then provider label, then model label. That is model-domain logic living inside a page.

The builtin command list is stated three times, at `ChatView.tsx:34-40`, in the `/help` text at `Session.tsx:266-274`, plus the switch arms at `Session.tsx:276-342`. Those three copies can drift apart.

Suggested restructuring. Move the sort into `models/sessionModels.ts` as `sortModelsForSelection(...)`. Move `handleCommand` into `session/slashCommands.ts` as one registry of `{ name, description, run }`, shared by `ChatView` plus `Session`. Split `updateSessionModel` into a pure mutation plus a caller-side announcement.

### F12. useAgentStream conjoins queueing, cancellation, plus two transports (severity: med)

See `hooks/useAgentStream.ts:35-215`. Three functions cannot be read independently. `sendPrompt` (`:200-222`) writes `queuedPromptRef` then calls `cancel` (`:180-198`). The `finally` block of `startPrompt` (`:161-177`) then re-invokes `startPrompt` for the queued prompt. Understanding one function requires reading the other two, which is the conjoined-methods flag.

The recursive re-entry at `:172-176` is also nonobvious. `startPrompt` calls itself from its own `finally` block with no depth bound. Repeated steering builds an implicit chain.

`upsertTurn` plus `scheduleUpsert` (`:70-108`) implement rAF-batched message coalescing inside the same closure. That is a separate, testable concern.

Suggested restructuring. Model the run lifecycle as an explicit reducer over `idle | running | stopping`, an enum that already exists at `:33`. Hold the queued prompt inside that state rather than in a ref read from a `finally` block. Extract the rAF batching into `utils/turnBuffer.ts`.

### F13. Dead and inert code (severity: low)

`components/ChatView.tsx:78` declares `showMenu`. It is written at `:146`, `:197`, `:208`, plus `:238`, and it is never read. `menuVisible` (`:141`) is derived from `slashFilter` with `filteredCommands`. Delete the state plus its four setters.

`components/ChatView.tsx:211` lists `streaming` as a `handleSubmit` dependency. The body at `:180-210` never references it.

`api/client.ts:515-579` plus the branches at `useAgentStream.ts:120-134` and `:186-195` are unreachable, as covered in F8. `runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:324-327` validates an upload path that is never requested, as covered in F7.

### F14. Comment and naming observations (severity: low)
